title: Evaluation of a multiplex PCR method to serotype Salmonella in animal feeds pre-enrichment broth cultures
author: Jean-Gilles Beaubrun, Ewing, et al.
materials: •One ml of samples after 24 h pre-enrichment. The samples were collected in a 1.5 ml sterile Eppendorf microcentrifudge tube.•The tubes were centrifuged at 10,000 g for 10 min•DNA was purified from the 24 h pellets using Roche MagNA Pure Compact (Roche, Indianapolis IN) according to the manufacturer’s instructions.•DNA extraction quality and the PCR serotyping outcome are amplified by collecting samples at 24 h after inoculation. (Note: An important factor in the success of this assay is the ability to extract the DNA from the different matrices).•The broth used for the pre-enrichment (Lactose or mBPW) showed no significant difference in recovery of Salmonella. Although the mBPW seems to be a better growth media for Salmonella in various matrices [11], in the animal feed it did not make a major difference.

The PCR method consisted of two five-plex PCR reactions and one two-plex PCR reaction; the primers for each of the reactions are listed in Table 1, Table 2.•The PCR master mix contained 5.0 μl of Q buffer, 5.0 μl of 10× Tris-Borate-EDTA buffer, 5.0 μl of 25 mM MgCl2 (Qiagen, Inc., Valencia, CA), 5.0 μl of a 10 mM concentration of the deoxynucleoside triphosphates (Invitrogen Corporation, Carlsbad, CA), 0.5 μl of HotStar Taq (Qiagen, Inc.) and 5.0 mM of each primer.•PCR amplification of each sample was conducted using 2.0 μl of DNA template, and 48 μl of a master mix containing primers, for a total volume of 50 μl.•The amplification parameters were as follows: a 5 min step at 94 °C, followed by 40 amplification cycles that consisted of a 30 s denaturing step at 94 °C, a 30 s annealing step at 56 °C, and a 1 min elongation step at 72 °C, and a final extension step of 5 min [11].•Inhibitory factors may interfere with PCR results.•Lack of Salmonella growth in this particular feed may also minimize detection by PCR•Table 3 show that each feed type is different and the growth obtained from each feed also differed.Table 3A summary of the limit of detection study of the Horse steps.title: Collect sample and extract DNA
steps.instruction: Take 1 mL of each 24 h pre‑enrichment broth sample, place it in a sterile 1.5 mL Eppendorf tube, centrifuge at 10 000 g for 10 min, and purify DNA from the pellet using the Roche MagNA Pure Compact system following the manufacturer’s instructions.

steps.title: Prepare master mix for primer set 1
steps.instruction: For each 50 µL reaction of the first five‑plex PCR, combine: 5 µL Q Buffer, 5 µL 10× TBE Buffer, 5 µL 25 mM MgCl₂ (Qiagen), 7 µL 10 mM dNTPs, 2.5 µL primer mix (final 0.25 mM per primer), 0.5 µL HotStar Taq (1000 U), 23 µL nuclease‑free water. Do not add DNA template yet.

steps.title: Prepare master mix for primer set 2
steps.instruction: For each 50 µL reaction of the second five‑plex PCR, combine: 5 µL Q Buffer, 5 µL 10× TBE Buffer, 5 µL 25 mM MgCl₂ (Qiagen), 7 µL 10 mM dNTPs, 2.5 µL primer mix (final 0.25 mM per primer), 0.5 µL HotStar Taq (1000 U), 23 µL nuclease‑free water. Do not add DNA template yet.

steps.title: Prepare master mix for primer set 3
steps.instruction: For each 50 µL reaction of the two‑plex PCR, combine: 5 µL Q Buffer, 5 µL 10× TBE Buffer, 5 µL 25 mM MgCl₂ (Qiagen), 7 µL 10 mM dNTPs, 1 µL primer mix (final 0.10 mM per primer), 0.5 µL HotStar Taq (1000 U), 24 µL nuclease‑free water. Do not add DNA template yet.

steps.title: Add DNA template to master mixes
steps.instruction: To each prepared 48 µL master mix (sets 1‑3), add 2 µL of the extracted DNA template to obtain a final reaction volume of 50 µL.

steps.title: Run PCR amplification
steps.instruction: Place the 50 µL reactions in a thermal cycler and run: 5 min at 94 °C; 40 cycles of 30 s at 94 °C, 30 s at 56 °C, 1 min at 72 °C; then a final extension of 5 min at 72 °C.

steps.title: Analyze PCR products on Bioanalyzer
steps.instruction: Load each PCR product onto an Agilent 2100 Bioanalyzer using the DNA 1000 Reagents kit, following the manufacturer’s protocol, and acquire the electropherogram/gel‑like image to assess serotype‑specific banding patterns.
